bullets.text: The eastern section of the Kessel Embankment failed by overtopping, flooding around 8,000 hectares of cropland and the farming village of Marnow, and driving the river to its highest level since 1998.
Six people died and about 45,000 were displaced at the peak, with major losses to the standing rice crop, cattle and the Pelley Hook fishing fleet in a region dependent on farming and fishing.
A 48-hour forecast enabled precautionary evacuations before landfall; after the storm the response shifted to boat rescue, safe water, disease surveillance and slow drainage of the breached blocks.
KMD issues a 48-hour landfall forecast for Cyclone Vessa and warns of serious flood risk on the swollen Osel River.
The Bramwick district office orders precautionary evacuation of char islands and riverside hamlets; NDRC pre-positions 40 rescue boats and supplies.
Precautionary evacuation of char islands and riverside hamlets was ordered roughly two days before landfall, with boats running from the Pelley Hook jetty.
The compound hazard combined cyclone winds around 110 km/h with 200-300 mm of rain falling on an already monsoon-swollen river.
The district ran precautionary evacuations, opened 62 shelters, and shifted public communication to radio when networks failed.
KMD issued a 48-hour landfall forecast and flood-risk warning, giving the delta a genuine preparation window.
